reviewer: Codex in the interactive subscription session; reviewed against original source pages, no paid grader calls

city-01-1.rationale: Pages 4–5 require sprinklering, smoke detection, CO alarm and emergency lighting and flag the starred issues as serious. The post preserves building-review attribution.

city-01-2.rationale: Page 4 names all four systems for the existing one-storey building; page 5 identifies serious non-conformities. The post invents no installation deadline.

city-01-3.rationale: Pages 4–5 support these concrete fire-safety requirements and their serious-issue flag. At building review identifies the review context rather than claiming completion before the development permit.

city-02-1.rationale: Pages 3–4 require underground utility services and wholly private-property electrical equipment. The post states the physical demand without an invented construction deadline.

city-02-2.rationale: Pages 1–2 establish the heritage hotel project, removal OR relocation of existing encroaching swings, and a 0.3 m maximum for new emergency-exit swings. Both alternative and maximum survive.

city-02-3.rationale: Page 2 supports both alternatives for existing encroaching door swings and the 0.3 m cap for new emergency exits. Specific, readable and fully qualified.

blocking_issues: A generic contingent contaminated-site covenant displaces the actual public-plaza access and street works.
city-03-1.rationale: Pages 13–14 describe a covenant if required, without establishing that this site triggers it. This conditional administrative clause is a weaker lead than the concrete project obligations on pages 5 and 9.

city-03-2.rationale: Page 5 requires arrangements securing public use rights over the private plaza before permit issuance. Securing rights describes the arrangements without expressly asserting completed registration.

city-03-3.rationale: Page 5 requires arrangements for public use rights over the proposed private plaza. The post describes legal public access without asserting completed registration or an already open plaza.

city-04-1.rationale: Page 3 bans amplified music and live entertainment in and around the patio at all times. The outdoor scope and absolute time restriction survive.

city-04-2.rationale: Page 3 supports the patio entertainment ban at all times, rather than an indoor or closing-time-only ban.

city-04-3.rationale: Page 3 prohibits amplified music and live entertainment in and around the patio at any time. The post preserves the outdoor scope and all-times restriction.

city-05-1.rationale: Page 3 explicitly demands removal of surface parking, and page 4 identifies the conflict with the minimum 6.1 m garage aisle. This reports removal without suggesting that the Engineering alternative overrides the Urban Design condition.

city-05-2.rationale: Pages 6–7 classify this as reconstruction and explicitly require sprinklers throughout the building. Building-review attribution preserves the stage.

city-05-3.rationale: Page 5 requires consolidation arrangements for Lot 17 and specifically the east half of Lot 18. The post preserves the partial-lot boundary and adds no premature completion deadline.

city-06-1.rationale: Page 5 assigns design and payment for street upgrades to the owner at no City cost, including the minimum 3 m Fraser sidewalk and duct banks.

city-06-2.rationale: Page 5 supports both minimum sidewalk widths and new duct banks. At least applies to the coordinated widths, and owner payment is explicit.

city-06-3.rationale: Page 5 names a minimum 2.1 m E 24th sidewalk, curb ramp, lane crossing and new duct banks at no City cost. The post preserves the minimum and correctly assigns payment to the owner.

city-07-1.rationale: Page 2 places the specified encroachment agreements before permit issuance and identifies existing Keefer cornices/bay windows plus proposed lane gutter/drainpipe. Their concrete scope is retained.

city-07-2.rationale: Page 2 supports agreements for the named street and lane projections. The legal demand is explained through the actual structures rather than generic paperwork.

city-07-3.rationale: Page 2 requires the named encroachment agreements for cornices, bay windows and proposed lane gutter/drainpipe. Concise and scoped to the source.

city-08-1.rationale: Pages 4–5 explicitly require two-hour fire separation between daycare outdoor space and the adjacent garbage/recycling room. No installation deadline is invented.

city-08-2.rationale: Pages 4–5 support the two-hour separation and adjacent residential garbage/recycling room, correctly attributed to later building review.

city-08-3.rationale: Page 5 requires the two-hour separation between the outdoor play space and neighbouring garbage/recycling room. Repetition of separation/separating is inelegant but the demand is clear.

city-09-1.rationale: Page 5 requires a designated egress path for stair 2 and warns of playground tripping hazards during evacuation. It does not invent a specific route or require avoiding the entire playground.

city-09-3.rationale: Page 5 supports the designated exit path and playground evacuation hazard. Building review preserves the later stage.

city-10-1.rationale: Pages 5–6 tie the daycare change to structural assessment/code analysis and whole-building upgrade requirements including sprinklers. The post names actual investigations and building-wide scope without moving construction before the development permit.

city-10-2.rationale: Pages 5–6 require structural assessment and whole-building sprinkler/exit upgrades at later building review. Concrete work and investigation replace unexplained upgrade codes.

city-11-1.rationale: Page 5 specifies public pedestrian access beside Main Street with a 2.5 m offset from the property line. The post conveys a quantified land-access demand without claiming completed registration.

city-11-2.rationale: Page 5 requires the 2.5 m public-access offset free of at-grade obstructions and separately accommodates underground parking. The post does not make the parking a cause of the access requirement.

city-11-3.rationale: Page 5 supports public pedestrian rights within a 2.5 m property-line offset, clear at grade of walls, stairs and vents.

city-12-1.rationale: Pages 4–5 require plans protecting six neighbouring trees and addressing root conflicts. The post reports design work rather than universally imposing one foundation method.

city-12-2.rationale: Page 3 caps the rear building at 25.26 ft/7.7 m and identifies a 2.2 ft excess. The post correctly asks for revised plans, not completed construction before the permit.

city-12-3.rationale: Page 4 requires protection of six off-site trees and identifies foundation/shoring/tunnelling methods as examples. Using fixes like preserves the optional choice of method.

focused-duration-1.rationale: Pages 1–2 require arrangements securing rental tenure for all 12 residential units for the longer of 60 years or building life, excluding the shop. The duration, scope and arrangements stage survive.

focused-duration-2.rationale: Pages 1–2 support all twelve rental-housing units for the longer of 60 years or building life through the Housing Agreement/covenant. The rental-housing context identifies the residential units rather than the separate commercial unit.

focused-duration-3.rationale: Pages 1–2 support 12 residential units, the longer-of duration and explicit commercial exclusion. No construction deadline is invented.

focused-security-1.rationale: Pages 1–2 require $250,000 letter-of-credit security OR an approved alternative, returned following acceptance. All material qualifications survive despite slightly awkward alternative placement.

focused-security-2.rationale: Pages 1–2 support the amount, before-permit security, return on acceptance and approved alternative. It is not called a fee or mandatory cash payment.

focused-security-3.rationale: Pages 1–2 support $250,000 in returnable security, letter of credit OR approved alternative, before the development permit. This clearly distinguishes security from a fee.
